issues_outside_coverage: Capital loss limitation under section 1211(b): $123,822 net long-term capital loss limited to $3,000, excess carried forward to 2018 under section 1212(b); Schedule D 'if-then-else' reading rejected; forms/instructions do not control over the statute
Overpayment/refund claim after a section 6213(b) math error assessment that was paid without requesting abatement (jurisdiction under sections 6214(a) and 6512(b)); no overpayment
Tuition and fees deduction (Form 8917, section 222) of $4,000 allowed by the IRS during examination (not contested)
Hardship/collection alternatives (installment agreement, offer-in-compromise) are for the IRS, not this proceeding
decisive_judgment_findings: Parties agreed the net long-term capital loss was $123,822 and that petitioners paid the math error assessment without seeking abatement
Household consisted of petitioners and one child claimed as an exemption; the child was not required to file and had no income (family size three)
Petitioners received $13,982 Social Security benefits, of which $2,097 was nontaxable and included in modified AGI
Monthly APTC of $1,471 was paid for each month of 2017
